Manjunatha D. V: 
Thank you. Good evening, everyone. I extend a warm welcome to all our investors, analysts, and 
shareholders joining us on Emmvee's Q2 and H1 financial year '27 earnings conference call. I am 
pleased to share that Emmvee has delivered its strongest half-yearly financial performance to date. 
For the first half of financial year '27, our revenue from operation grew by 45% year-on-year to 
INR3,132 crores. EBITDA increased by 47% to INR1,105 crores. 
 
The profit after tax grew by 79% to INR762 crores. We have maintained EBITDA margins of 
approximately 35%, demonstrating the strength and consistency of our operating performance. These 
results reflect the manufacturing capabilities we have developed over nearly two decades, our 
continued focus on technology and product reliability, and the trust we have built with our customers.  
 
Importantly, our performance has remained consistent with the guidance we provided, even as the 
industry transitioned through changes in the implementation of ALMM regulations and geopolitical 
issues. Our focus has remained on executing our business plans, strengthening our manufacturing 
capabilities, and delivering sustainable growth. Let me now share our perspective on the Indian solar 
industry.  
Indian solar sector continue to experience significant growth, supported by increasing electricity 
demand, renewable energy commitment, and the continued development of solar projects across 
multiple segments. The first half of calendar year 2027 has witnessed India's highest-ever solar 
installation for a 6-month period. 
Based on the current installation trajectory, domestic module demand is running a pace that could 
translate into approximately 64% year-on-year growth for this year. This is a significant development 
for the domestic manufacturing industry. We are seeing demand across utility-scale projects, 
commercial, industrial installations, rooftop solar, and government-supported programs. 
In addition, the growing adoption of hybrid, round-the-clock, and firm renewable energy projects is 
creating more module demand as the AC-DC ratios increase in these solar deployments. As India's 
energy requirements grow, we expect solar to continue playing an increasingly important role in the

country's electricity generation mix.  
At the same time, the domestic manufacturing ecosystem is evolving. The implementation of ALMM-
II for solar cell is an important step towards strengthening India's domestic manufacturing capabilities. 
While certain transitional provisions have been introduced, the broader direction of the policy 
continued to support greater domestic value addition and deeper integration across solar 
manufacturing supply chain. 
Emmvee is well-positioned to participate in the transition, supported by our existing TOPCon cell 
manufacturing capabilities, established module manufacturing operations, and continued investment 
in integration. Our inclusion in G12R TOPCon cells under ALMM List-II further strengthened our 
ability to serve evolving customer requirements.  
Coming to our ongoing expansion, our 6 gigawatt integrated TOPCon cell and module manufacturing 
project remain on track. We expect the commissioning of the module manufacturing facility by 
December, followed by cell manufacturing facility by March 2027. Upon completion, our total 
installed manufacturing capacity will increase to approximately 16.3 gigawatt of modules and 8.9 
gigawatt of cells. 
An important aspect of our manufacturing strategy is how these capacities have been designed to 
operate together. Cell and module manufacturing have different operating characteristics. Cell 
manufacturing can achieve significantly higher utilization level, whereas module manufacturing 
requires greater flexibility to accommodate different product configurations, customer specifications, 
and production schedules.  
When we consider the maximum achievable production for both operations, our 16.3 gigawatt of 
module capacity and 8.9 gigawatt of cell capacity are designed to deliver broadly equivalent annual 
output. This is central to our integrated manufacturing strategy. Our objective is to optimize the 
utilization of our manufacturing and strengthening our cost competitiveness. 
We believe that manufacturing integration must be evaluated not simply by installing capacity, but by 
the ability of different stages of production to operate efficiently together. Beyond our ongoing 
expansion, we are also progressing with our plans for backward integration into ingot and wafer 
manufacturing. 
Our current plan envisages a 9 gigawatt of facility developed in two phases of 5 gigawatt and 4 
gigawatt, aligned with our future cell manufacturing requirements. The timing of this investment will 
be guided by the regulatory development, particularly ALMM List-III, prevailing market condition, 
and long-term economic viability. 
Our approach to expansion remained disciplined. We believe the next phase of growth in Indian solar 
manufacturing will increasingly depend on technological capabilities, manufacturing efficiency, 
product reliability, and supply chain integration. These are areas in which Emmvee has consistently 
invested over the years. 
Our collaboration with leading research institutions, our experience in TOPCon cell manufacturing 
and our focus on product quality provide a strong foundation for the future. As we enter the second 
half of financial year 2027, our priorities remain clear. We will continue to execute our expansion

continue to place considerable emphasis on working capital management, particularly inventory 
planning, receivables, and cash generation. As our operations scale, we are focused on ensuring that

facilities.

manufacturing capacity. Third, we will continue to strengthen our customer relationship, execute our 
order book, and improve our product and technology capabilities. And finally, we will remain focused
